st7735.aria: Diagram of eight wires between the 80 by 160 ST7735 TFT and the Pulsar C5
st7735.scrollHint: Swipe the diagram to the right to see the display.

start.title: Unplug USB before wiring
start.text: Press Next to see each connection, or Show all to display them together.

notes.GND: Connect the screen and board grounds.
notes.VCC: Power the TFT from 3V3; do not use 5 V.
notes.SCL: SCL is the screen's SPI clock. Connect it to D13 / GPIO27, not QWIIC SCL.
notes.SDA: SDA is the screen's SPI MOSI input. Connect it to D11 / GPIO7, not QWIIC SDA.
notes.CS: Display chip select: D4 / GPIO9. This leaves A1 / GPIO1 free for QWIIC SDA.
notes.DC: Data or command select: A2 / GPIO4.
notes.BLK: Share the 3V3 rail with VCC, for example on a breadboard, to power the backlight. Leave BLK open if your module already connects it internally.

preview.aria: Simulated 320 by 170 display: colour check, then a moving sine wave

captions.check: Step 1: colour check (2.5 s). Left to right must read red, green, blue.
captions.scope: Step 2: the bench scope. Your real screen runs it at 22 fps.

wiring.aria: Wiring diagram: 8 jumper wires from the display header to the ESP32 left header

start.title: Unplug USB first
start.text: Then press Play, or Next to place one wire at a time.

done.text: Double-check VCC is on 3V3. Press Signals to see what travels on each wire.

wires.GND: Ground first. Both boards need the same 0 V reference, or no signal makes sense.
wires.VCC: Power for the screen. Use 3V3, not 5V: the ESP32's pins speak 3.3 V.
wires.SCL: SPI clock. The ESP ticks this line once per bit, 40 million times a second.
wires.SDA: SPI data (MOSI). The bits themselves: the screen reads one on every clock tick.
wires.RES: Reset. Pulled low once at start-up to reboot the screen's controller chip.
wires.DC: Data/Command. Low means the byte is a command, high means it is pixel data.
wires.CS: Chip select. Low means “I'm talking to you”. Lets several devices share one SPI bus.
wires.BLK: Backlight. High switches the light on. Without it the screen looks dead even while drawing.

analyzer.aria: Logic analyzer view of one SPI transfer

notes.low: pixel data, low byte → 0xF800 = one red pixel

analyzer.still: SCL stays still, nothing is sent
analyzer.switching: DC switches between command and data

both.title: 10 wires on one header
both.text: 8 go to the screen (an output), 2 go to the button (an input). Both need a GND; any GND pin works. Pin 5 sits right next to 4, so check the label.

screen.title: Screen: an output on 8 wires
screen.text: Power (VCC, GND), the SPI bus (SCL, SDA), and control lines (CS, DC, RES, BLK). Data flows from the ESP32 to the screen, millions of bits a second.

button.title: Button: an input on 2 wires
button.text: GPIO 5 and GND. No power wire: the chip's internal pull-up holds GPIO 5 HIGH, and pressing joins it to GND (LOW). Press the button to see the signal travel in.

full.aria: The ESP32 left header with the display wired to 8 pins and the push button wired to GPIO 5 and GND
full.out: OUT → ESP32 talks to the screen
full.in: IN ← ESP32 listens to the button
full.gnd: screen and button GND: any GND pin works

button.aria: Inside a 4-leg push button, and how it sits on the breadboard wired to GPIO 5 and GND
button.joined: A–C and B–D are always joined.

pressed.title: Pressed: GPIO 5 joined to GND
pressed.text: The pin is pulled to 0 V, so it reads LOW. The internal pull-up only leaks a tiny current.

released.title: Released: the pull-up holds the pin HIGH
released.text: A resistor inside the chip connects GPIO 5 to 3.3 V, so an open button reads HIGH. Press and hold the button above.

button.scopeAria: Signal on GPIO 5: raw with bounce, and debounced

canvas.zoom: ZOOM: first 7 ms of the press

scope.traces: The yellow line is what the pin really does; green is what the program trusts.
scope.try: Try a click, a double-click and a long press.
scope.debounce: debounce waits {{ms}} ms of quiet before trusting a change

direction.label: Direction
direction.screen: Output. The ESP32 sends; the screen only listens.
direction.button: Input. The ESP32 listens; the button only reports.

wires.label: Wires
wires.screen: 8: VCC + GND for power, SCL + SDA for data, CS, DC, RES, BLK for control

power.label: Power
power.screen: Needs 3V3 from the board to light up
power.button: None. A button is just a switch

signal.label: Signal
signal.screen: SPI bus: a clock (SCL) and data (SDA), 40 million bits per second
signal.button: One level: HIGH (up) or LOW (pressed), a few changes per second

pins.label: Which pins
pins.screen: SCL/SDA on the S3's fast SPI pins 12/11; the other 4 on any safe GPIO

helper.label: Helper inside the chip
helper.screen: The SPI peripheral clocks the bits out for us
helper.button: The internal pull-up resistor keeps the pin HIGH until pressed

wrong.label: If it goes wrong
wrong.screen: Black or white screen: check VCC, BLK, RES
wrong.button: Always or never pressed: use diagonal legs

showcase.terminal: $ uv run pio device monitor   (expected output)

boot.aria: BOOT button: click for next scene, hold for auto-cycle
boot.caption: Click BOOT for the next scene, hold 0.6 s to toggle auto-cycle, just like the real BOOT button. The dashboard here uses placeholder numbers; your board shows its real temperature, memory and frame times.

button.aria: Push button: click for next scene, double-click for previous, hold for auto-cycle
button.caption: Click BUTTON for the next scene, double-click for the previous one, hold 0.6 s to toggle auto-cycle, just like your push button. The dashboard here uses placeholder numbers; your board shows its real temperature, memory and frame times.

oled.aria: The Pulsar C5 turned with USB-C down. A QWIIC cable runs from its QWIIC port to the UNIT QWIIC Bus hub, and the SSD1306 OLED plugs into the hub: SDA on GPIO1, SCL on GPIO6, 3.3 V and ground. A1 and A6 on the header carry the same SDA and SCL.
oled.title: Plug and play: one cable carries everything
oled.text: The QWIIC cable brings 3.3 V, ground and the I²C pair (SDA on GPIO1, SCL on GPIO6) to the hub, and the OLED answers at 0x3C. A1 and A6 on the header are the same two lines, if you wire with jumpers instead.

sd.aria: The Pulsar C5 turned with USB-C down and a card in its microSD slot. The slot uses four header pads: CS on D5 (GPIO23), MOSI on D11 (GPIO7), MISO on D12 (GPIO26) and SCK on D13 (GPIO27).
sd.title: Already wired on the board
sd.text: The slot is connected to these four pads under the board: there is nothing to wire. While a card is in use, keep D5, D11, D12 and D13 free, because anything you connect to them shares the card's SPI lines.

imu.aria: The Pulsar C5 turned with USB-C down. A QWIIC cable runs from its QWIIC port, round the left and up into the QWIIC connector at the bottom of the BMI270 breakout: SDA on GPIO1, SCL on GPIO6, 3.3 V and ground. The breakout's edge pads are ASDx, ASCx, INT1, INT2, OCSB and OSDO on the left, GND, VCC, SDA, SCL, SDO and CS on the right.
imu.title: One cable, no soldering
imu.text: The QWIIC cable plugs straight into the BMI270 breakout, which answers at 0x68 (0x69 if its SDO pad is tied high). Its edge pads are for SPI, interrupts and an extra sensor: D1 needs none of them.

light.aria: The Pulsar C5 turned with USB-C down. A QWIIC cable runs to the UNIT QWIIC Bus hub. The SSD1306 OLED plugs into the hub's pins and shows a light graph, and a short QWIIC cable from the hub's other port goes to the DevLab TEMT6000 light sensor board.
light.title: Two parts, one bus
light.text: The TFT can stay connected with CS on D4/GPIO9. If your older hookup has CS on A1/GPIO1, unplug USB and move that one wire to D4. QWIIC then uses GPIO1 for SDA and GPIO6 for SCL; the OLED answers at 0x3C and the TEMT6000 DDP at 0x20.
